context.body: I saw, in the right hand of him who sat on the throne, a book written inside and outside, sealed shut with seven seals.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: A sealed scroll prompts weeping until an elder announces the Lion of Judah and Root of David has overcome; the seer then sees a slain-standing Lamb who takes the scroll and receives a new song.
observations.label: The Root of David is announced before a Lamb appears: textual observation

observations.body: The passage keeps the throne sitter, mighty angel, seer, elder, Lion, Root of David, Lamb, creatures, and elders, the heavenly throne room and sealed scroll, holding, searching, weeping, announcing victory, seeing a slain Lamb, taking the scroll, falling down, and singing visible within David's story or later memory.
observations.label: The Root of David is announced before a Lamb appears: action, promise, or consequence

observations.body: the throne sitter, mighty angel, seer, elder, Lion, Root of David, Lamb, creatures, and elders · the heavenly throne room and sealed scroll · holding, searching, weeping, announcing victory, seeing a slain Lamb, taking the scroll, falling down, and singing · what is heard as lion and root is seen as a slain-standing Lamb
observations.label: Relationships named in Revelation 5:1–10

payload.posture: Read Revelation 5:1–10 as its own gospel and apostolic memory David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places what is heard as lion and root is seen as a slain-standing Lamb inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
payload.title: The Root of David is announced before a Lamb appears
